subject: SOC 2 applicability across hosting modes & bridge letter request
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-retail.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 coverage question + bridge letter request

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme is moving quickly on a pilot and procurement asked for a couple things I wanted to confirm before we proceed: 

1) Does Redwood's SOC 2 Type II (most recent) cover Dedicated reserved pools (Redwood-managed) as well as Hosted API? We are planning to use Redwood Hosted for our public-facing features and a Dedicated pool for high-volume inference for internal product teams.

2) We also have a procurement requirement to get a bridge letter covering the audit period Jan 1 2025 – Dec 31 2025 confirming there were no significant control exceptions. Can Redwood provide a signed bridge letter we can share with our vendor risk team?

3) If Dedicated is included, are there specific artifacts we should request (tenant-isolation, encryption-in-transit, KMS integration screenshots)? We also have a SIG questionnaire in progress — any guidance on which items Redwood typically answers vs items we should mark as "customer responsibility" for Dedicated/VPC deployments would help.

Attached is our vendor intake form (small) and the SIG extract relevant to hosting.

Appreciate quick confirmation — procurement is asking to close this in the next few business days.

Best,
Sophie Lang
Security & Vendor Risk | Acme Retail
attachments: Acme_VendorForm.pdf, SIG-extract.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-retail.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question + bridge letter request

Hi Sophie — thanks for sending this over and congrats on the fast timeline. Quick answers up front then details/follow-ups below:

- Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) covers our Hosted API and Redwood-managed Dedicated pools.
- Customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployments (private installs where the customer controls the infrastructure) are out of scope for Redwood's SOC 2 attestation — those are considered customer-hosted.
- We can provide a signed bridge letter for the audit period you specified.

Neha (cc'd) will send the SOC 2 PDF and a draft bridge letter and confirm the typical artifact list for Dedicated coverage. Laura (cc'd, compliance) will help with any procurement rubric/language you want in the vendor record.

One clarifying question for your team: when you say "Dedicated pool" — is that Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity managed by Redwood and logically isolated for Acme) or are you planning to self-host in your VPC? If it's the former, we can include it in the scope.

I can also put you in touch with our security engineer if you want a quick sync.

—Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-retail.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question + bridge letter request

Hi Sophie — happy to help. Attaching: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf and draft_bridge_letter_acme.docx and a scope_matrix_hosting_modes.csv that maps hosting modes to coverage/responsibility. Attachments included in this thread.

A few specifics pulled from the scope matrix:
- Hosted API: Fully in-scope for SOC 2 controls we attest to (CC1–CC8 as applicable).
- Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated GPU pools / reserved capacity): Included in scope provided the Dedicated environment is provisioned and managed by Redwood (tenant isolation, network controls, key management stay under Redwood operational control).
- VPC / on-prem (customer-managed): Out-of-scope; we provide implementation guidance but these are the customer's responsibility for operational controls.

Audit period covered by the attached SOC 2 Type II: 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31. The report covers control testing across that period; the bridge letter will affirm there were no material exceptions identified after the report issuance date for that period (standard limited-scope statement).

Common artifacts Acme may request for Redwood-managed Dedicated:
- Tenant isolation diagram + network segmentation screenshots
- KMS/HSM integration confirmation and key rotation cadence
- Sample alerting/tracing for model-serving hosts (obfuscated tenant ids)
- Encryption-in-transit configs (TLS versions, ciphers)
- Patch management cadence + an example patch runbook

For SIG/CAIQ: we'll answer items that map to Redwood-run controls. Anything that requires customer configuration in a VPC or on-prem install we mark as "customer responsibility" and provide guidance text.

If you confirm Dedicated is Redwood-managed, we'll:
1) Send a signed PDF of the bridge letter (we'll route to legal for signature).
2) Provide the SOC 2 PDF (attached).
3) Share the artifact checklist and a short explanation for each item to expedite procurement review.

Would you like the bridge letter signed and returned, or a redline-friendly Word doc so procurement/legal can attach it to their vendor portal?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf, draft_bridge_letter_acme.docx, scope_matrix_hosting_modes.csv

From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-retail.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-retail.com, Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question + bridge letter request

Thanks Neha — this is helpful. To confirm: Acme will consume a Redwood-managed Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) — not self-hosting. Procurement also asked for two additional confirmations:

- Can you explicitly confirm that tenant isolation controls for Redwood Dedicated are tested as part of the SOC 2 period? (They want wording we can paste into their vendor risk system.)
- For KMS, we use our own customer-managed keys for certain data flows — how does Redwood handle customer-supplied keys for Dedicated pools? Is that supported or would we need a Private/VPC deployment for full control?

Procurement prefers a signed PDF bridge letter; please send that and a short artifact packet we can upload. If you have a single page "scope statement" we can store alongside the bridge letter that would be ideal.

Best,
Sophie

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-retail.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question + bridge letter request

Sophie — quick confirmations:

- Tenant isolation for Redwood-managed Dedicated pools is included in the SOC 2 testing scope during the audit period; Neha's attached scope matrix has suggested wording you can paste into your vendor portal.
- Regarding KMS: Redwood supports KMS integration for key management on our managed services. For Dedicated pools we can integrate with customer KMS in many cases but there are limitations depending on the specific key custody model — if Acme requires full control of keys within your own HSM (customer-hosted KMS), that typically pushes toward a Private/VPC deployment. Neha can flag the exact matrix entry.

We'll route the draft bridge letter through legal and deliver a signed PDF. Laura — can you prepare a one-page scope statement we can attach?

—Vivek
